heading: AUDIENCES DON'T WANT MORE FOOTAGE. THEY WANT IN (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article argues that entertainment franchises are misunderstanding fan engagement by producing more content when audiences actually want participatory opportunities. It cites Deloitte data showing 70% of hardcore video game fans want franchise extensions into other media—not more of the same product—and notes the Grand Theft Auto VI trailer generated over 186 million fan responses through reactions, theories, and edits, more than double its 93 million official views. While companion podcasts demonstrate that fans want to stay engaged between releases, they function as broadcast rather than true participation, leaving franchises unprepared to let audiences actively shape the worlds they love. The article suggests that technology has made fan participation at scale newly affordable, yet most franchises continue to fill the gap between releases with passive content consumption rather than building participatory layers where fans can engage, question, and shape stories.
strategic_hook: Understanding this shift from consumption to participation is essential for developing customer engagement strategies that align with how modern audiences—particularly younger, game-raised demographics—now expect to interact with brands and entertainment properties.

heading: THE SHIFT FROM SEO TO SOCIAL CONTENT (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: SEO's effectiveness as a lead source has declined sharply, with founders reporting drops from ten leads per week to five per month, driven by Google AI Overviews now appearing in 55% of searches and ranking #1 delivering 58% fewer clicks than previously. The shift reflects broader changes in buyer behavior, with 89% of B2B buyers now relying on GenAI tools like ChatGPT and Claude throughout their purchasing journey, and people increasingly turning to communities and social media rather than blog content. Rather than abandoning existing investments, the author advocates for "the great repurposing era," where companies convert their existing content libraries into social media formats—case studies into carousels, reports into infographics, articles into videos, and statistics into thought leadership posts. The recommended approach involves three steps: converting the entire content hub into a searchable AI knowledge center, creating a repurposing factory with a strategist, copywriter, and designer, and building internal discipline to ship zero-click, gated, and sales-enablement content weekly. Companies that invested in SEO content over the past 20 years now have the foundations for three years of social content if they execute the repurposing workflow.
strategic_hook: Understanding how shifts in customer search behavior and information-gathering preferences (from Google to GenAI to social platforms) fundamentally alter which content channels drive lead generation and should inform a company's go-to-market strategy and content investment priorities.

heading: TV ADS FOR B2B - WHY IT WORKS AND WHERE TO START (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Connected TV (CTV) advertising is an underutilized growth channel for B2B companies that can deliver measurable results starting with budgets as small as $50/day, according to Amit Sharan, SVP of Marketing at Tatari, whose platform generates over $100M in net revenue partly through CTV. Unlike social media, CTV offers 15-30 uninterrupted seconds to tell a brand story, making it effective for retargeting LinkedIn and website visitors once a company reaches approximately 10,000 unique monthly visitors. Successful CTV strategies involve repurposing existing content—including founder videos and customer case studies—rather than creating entirely new materials, with Tatari's top-performing format being a mashup of multiple customers reinforcing the same message. Companies running CTV ads report a 25% average increase in branded search and improved performance across other marketing channels, as brand recognition makes outreach and outbound efforts more effective. The article recommends treating CTV as a "channel in reserve" by allocating a portion of budget (such as 20%) to test and learn the platform now, ensuring it's ready to scale when growth pressure demands it, rather than attempting to quickly launch it under time constraints.
strategic_hook: Understanding how CTV advertising influences customer perception and brand recognition can inform customer-journey mapping by identifying when and how target customers encounter brand messaging across channels, which in turn supports the business case for channel diversification and budget allocation.

heading: I CAN'T BELIEVE SOME MARKETING TEAMS SKIP THIS (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: UserEvidence's VP of Marketing advocates for annual customer census surveys as a critical but underutilized marketing motion. The company conducts a single cross-functional survey (~13 questions) each summer to gather product feedback, sentiment, NPS scores, and customer testimonials—yielding over 50 new pieces of evidence annually. Success requires cross-functional planning with clear ownership of tradeoffs, thoughtful question design, targeted audience selection (UserEvidence narrowed to active users in editor roles), creative incentives (including charitable donation options), and rapid execution on results—the team published 16 customer assets, 18 G2 reviews, and secured 62 advocacy hand-raisers within one week of closing. The author emphasizes that marketing should own the census process because it generates customer evidence while building cross-functional relationships, and warns against launching during holidays or treating the survey as a one-time send rather than a campaign.
strategic_hook: Customer census surveys are a structured mechanism for discovering unmet customer needs, sentiment shifts, and competitive intelligence while simultaneously identifying advocates—making this directly applicable to customer research that informs positioning, sales enablement, and product strategy decisions.

heading: SAUCE (TOOL)
summary: Sauce is a new analytics tool that tracks how content published on off-site platforms like Reddit, YouTube, LinkedIn, and review sites gets cited by AI search engines including ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews. The platform allows teams to input their off-site content, define target search queries, and then monitor which pieces earn citations across six AI engines and 14 platforms, with attribution tracked by creator, post, and platform. A notable example shows B2B creator Kaleigh Moore's single LinkedIn article generating 130 AI citations. The tool is designed for SEO teams, community managers, social teams, and agencies trying to prove ROI and measure the search visibility impact of their off-site content strategy, with pricing starting at $49 per month for individuals and going up to $499 per month for multi-brand agency teams.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: BUILD A HERMES INBOX TRIAGER IN 90 MINS (10 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article provides a step-by-step tutorial for building an AI-powered email triage tool called Hermes in 90 minutes. The setup combines Hermes (an AI agent framework), Google AI Studio's Gemini 3.5 Flash model (free, no credit card required), Himalaya (a terminal-based email client for Gmail via IMAP), and Slack for notifications. The tool automatically reads unread emails, classifies them into five buckets—Action Needed, FYI, Noise, Subscriptions, and Needs Review—assigns urgency tiers (High/Medium/Low), moves or copies emails to labeled folders, and sends Slack alerts only for High-urgency messages. The implementation includes safeguards like processing one email at a time with rate-limit handling, preventing reprocessing through flagging, and routing uncertain emails to "Needs Review" rather than guessing.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: WHEN AI CHATBOTS BOOST VS HURT SALES (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Research from IÉSEG School of Management and University of Lille examined when AI chatbots help or hurt sales across four experiments involving 1,339 participants. The study found that chatbots boost purchase intention by 44.7% for products that are hard to evaluate (like clothing with multiple fit and style considerations), but reduce purchase intent for easy-to-evaluate products with small assortments (like a vitamin line with few options). For easy-to-evaluate products with large assortments (10+ options), chatbots increase engagement and purchase intent by helping customers navigate choice overload. The mechanism works because chatbots help customers manage ambiguity and uncertainty by structuring information, while conversational interaction mimics human interaction and increases engagement. The research was limited to a few product categories and did not account for chatbot design variations, recommendation accuracy, or implementation environment differences.
strategic_hook: A company considering chatbot implementation should first conduct customer research and product analysis to determine whether their catalog exhibits high evaluation complexity or choice overload, which determines whether a chatbot investment will meaningfully increase conversion versus waste resources.

heading: ANTHROPIC WILL PAY ITS NEW STANDARDS EDITOR $300K TO ARGUE ABOUT COMMAS (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Anthropic is hiring a Standards Editor at $300,000 annually to manage grammar, style, and tone across its public communications—the third such high-paid editorial hire among AI companies this year, following similar positions at Mercury ($335K), Vanta, Cohere, and LangChain. The role represents a market shift where AI companies recognize that as content generation becomes cheap, human judgment becomes expensive; Claude can produce countless grammatical versions of any text, but someone must make authoritative decisions about which version protects the brand. For Anthropic specifically, editorial standards function as core infrastructure since its $30 billion valuation rests on trust built through research posts, policy memos, and public communications rather than advertising. The underlying insight is that as AI-generated content converges on a "competent, recognizable, forgettable median," companies that sound distinct will be those paying for senior humans with authority to enforce brand voice and push back against algorithmic flatness.
strategic_hook: Understanding competitor strategy and positioning—Anthropic's willingness to pay surgeon-level salaries for editorial control signals that building differentiated brand voice through human judgment is becoming a core competitive capability, which should inform how other companies value and invest in their own editorial and brand functions.

heading: DJI USED GOPRO TO KILL GOPRO (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: In 2013, DJI launched its first consumer drone with a GoPro mount, leveraging GoPro's dominant brand to validate the emerging drone category without camera R&D. When GoPro founder Nick Woodman proposed a formal partnership offering GoPro two-thirds of profits in 2014, DJI CEO Frank Wang rejected it, arguing that drone flight technology—not cameras—was the genuine competitive moat. DJI immediately launched the Phantom 2 Vision+ with an integrated camera and shipped four successive generations over the next 30 months while GoPro developed its competing Karma drone. GoPro's Karma was recalled 16 days after launch due to mechanical failures and was discontinued entirely by January 2018, while DJI became the dominant drone manufacturer and eventually extended its category dominance into complementary products like Osmo cameras and DJI Mics for vloggers.
strategic_hook: Competitive analysis should identify whether partnership offers undervalue your core competitive advantage, and market timing analysis should recognize when iterative speed creates insurmountable leads during a competitor's delayed product launch window.

heading: HOW POLAROID IS WINNING GEN Z BY REJECTING AI AND SCREENS (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Polaroid has launched an anti-AI marketing campaign positioning itself as an alternative to digital culture, targeting Gen Z and millennials (ages 18-35) who comprise over 41% of instant photography consumers. The brand, revived in 2017 after early-2000s bankruptcy, reframed film's technical limitations—high cost, slow development, no editing—as premium benefits like mindfulness and authenticity. In 2025-2026, campaigns like "The Camera for an Analog Life" and "The Best of Summer Is Analog" placed billboards near Apple and Google offices while organizing phone-free walking tours in Paris, London, and Tokyo where participants used only Polaroid cameras. Rather than selling hardware, Polaroid promotes a lifestyle centered on physical memories and real-world experiences, leveraging the razor-and-blade business model where recurring film sales drive revenue. The strategy directly counters broader industry AI adoption by naming cultural anxieties about screen fatigue and AI-generated content while delivering a product that authentically delivers on that promise.
strategic_hook: Understanding Gen Z's emotional friction points around digital oversaturation and authenticity enables Polaroid to segment its market by psychographic cohorts (Creative Tastemakers vs. Analog Purists) and build a differentiated positioning that drives both hardware adoption and recurring film consumption.

heading: IS THE AGE OF READING ACTUALLY OVER? (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Ann Handley argues that The Atlantic's recent cover story declaring "the end of reading" is overstated and cherry-picks evidence to support an apocalyptic narrative. While acknowledging that reading formats have shifted toward short-form digital content, Handley points to counterevidence: print book sales are higher than a decade ago, Barnes & Noble opened 60+ new stores last year, nearly 400 independent bookstores opened in 2025, and readers actually spend more time reading daily than two decades ago. She distinguishes between reading fewer books and reading fewer words, noting Americans consume more written content than ever through news, social feeds, and articles. Handley argues that long-form reading has become more intentional and selective rather than extinct, and that we retain agency to choose what cognitive habits we strengthen. The piece concludes that reading is not dying but requires conscious cultivation as a deliberate practice in an accelerating world.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: CONTENT IS NO LONGER ENOUGH (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: The marketing industry's decade-long strategy of producing more content to gain visibility is exhausted in today's saturated digital ecosystem. At dentsu day 2026, leaders from the NFL, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Dentsu Creative argued that authenticity and belonging have become essential—not optional—and that brands must shift from content creation to community building. The panelists emphasized that audiences no longer want to simply consume stories; they want to belong to cultural ecosystems like Game of Thrones, Harry Potter, or the NFL that offer genuine connection and emotional refuge. Rather than chasing reach and impressions, brands should focus on understanding existing fan communities, co-creating with content creators and fans, and facilitating in-person experiences that deepen emotional bonds. The transformation requires moving beyond short-term metrics to build long-term cultural relevance, where content becomes the starting point rather than the end product of deeper relationships.
strategic_hook: Brands need to conduct community research and journey mapping to understand how existing fan ecosystems function, what emotional needs they fulfill, and where legitimate entry points exist for authentic partnership rather than interruptive messaging.

heading: +39% CONVERSIONS BY REMOVING A PROMINENT CALL-TO-ACTION (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: A global academic and professional editing service increased conversions by 39% by removing a prominent "Get Quote" call-to-action button from its homepage header. Research showed that visitors were clicking the button and jumping directly to a quote form that asked detailed questions (document type, service level, word count, turnaround time) they weren't yet prepared to answer, causing them to abandon the flow. By removing the button, visitors were forced to engage with the rest of the page, where they encountered service descriptions, team credentials, and trust signals that built confidence before encountering quote CTAs positioned on individual service pages. This demonstrates that a prominent early CTA can actually create friction by pushing users toward conversion before they have the knowledge and confidence needed to make an informed decision. The test validated what the firm calls the Safe Step Principle: visitors are more likely to continue when the next step feels appropriate to what they already know.
strategic_hook: This case illustrates the importance of customer-journey mapping and understanding where prospects are in their decision-making process—testing whether aggressive early conversion attempts may actually prevent sales by skipping necessary education and trust-building phases that different customer segments require.

heading: STOP MARKETING TO STRANGERS (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article argues that marketers are overinvesting in attracting new customers while neglecting the people who already know their brand. Using an anecdote about a locked golf simulator facility, the author illustrates how businesses lose existing prospects through small failures and argues that traditional marketing focuses too heavily on introductory "step-one" content rather than helping engaged audiences progress deeper. The piece proposes three solutions: create obvious next steps for returning visitors beyond generic calls-to-action, develop advanced content for long-term followers instead of repeating beginner material, and consistently deliver on small promises like accurate hours and working links. The author contends that loyalty is built and destroyed through incremental experiences, not dramatic moments, and that the marketing opportunity lies in serving known audiences rather than chasing strangers.
strategic_hook: Businesses should map the customer journey beyond initial awareness to identify friction points and unmet needs at deeper engagement stages, particularly for customers who have already demonstrated trust through previous interactions.

heading: USE AI TO FIND YOUR FASTEST ROUTE TO CULTURAL TRACTION (WEBINAR)
summary: Maven is hosting a free 30-minute webinar on July 23, 2026 titled "Use AI to Find Your Fastest Route to Cultural Traction," led by Vanina Schick, a former VP of Marketing and qualitative research expert. The session teaches marketers how to use AI to identify cultural conversations and moments where a brand's point of view gains organic attention, convert vanilla brand positioning into compelling viewpoints with cultural energy, and discover triggers and news topics to peg marketing campaigns to for earned attention. Schick positions the core problem as one of context: AI tools lack the human understanding of customer psychology and motivations, so she offers a proprietary method called "Marketing Alpha"—drawing on UX, strategy, and behavioral psychology frameworks—that provides AI with the business, product, and customer context needed to generate outputs beyond generic "slop." The underlying operational framework is called "Brand Governance" or technically "Context Engineering," which enables AI to understand the real-world and psychological experience of target customers.
strategic_hook: Marketers can use this approach to conduct market research and competitive analysis by deploying AI to map where their strategic positioning naturally appears in online conversations, revealing unmet customer needs and untapped cultural moments before competitors identify them.

heading: THE 2026 PAID PLAYBOOK: AUDIENCE, CHANNELS, AND AI (12 MINUTE READ)
summary: AI has collapsed the cost of paid marketing production, but the constraint has shifted from creative to audience targeting, channel selection, measurement rigor, and learning velocity. The article details a three-part playbook: building a durable audience advantage through identity resolution and CRM data layering (achieving 75% match rates on Meta versus 10-20% baseline), optimizing channel mix by persona rather than industry defaults (Reddit reaches IT at 70-80% but legal at 4%), and implementing causal measurement through holdout groups rather than relying on platform attribution models. Search is declining due to AI Overviews reducing clicks by 47%, making competitor-conquesting keywords and high-intent terms the surviving ROI drivers, while Meta and Reddit remain dramatically underpriced for B2B at $7-15 CPMs versus LinkedIn's $31-100+. The article emphasizes that competitive advantage now comes from who you target, where you reach them, how you measure incrementally, and how fast you learn—with emerging opportunities in thought-leader ads on LinkedIn, third-party influencer whitelisting, and experimental budget allocation to LLM-based ad platforms like ChatGPT starting at $60 CPMs.
strategic_hook: Understanding your buyer personas' actual channel behaviors and match rates across platforms—not industry defaults—directly informs where to allocate paid budget and how to prioritize customer acquisition channels in your go-to-market strategy.

heading: NETFLIX: THE BATTLE FOR ATTENTION (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Netflix faces a critical inflection point: it must now prove that a mature streaming business can sustain growth after walking away from a Warner Bros. Discovery merger and collecting a $2.8 billion breakup fee. Q2 FY26 results showed revenue of $12.6 billion (up 13% year-over-year) and a 33% operating margin, but the stock fell 8% after hours due to a narrowed—not raised—full-year outlook and expected Q3 revenue growth of only 12%, the slowest since 2023. To drive future growth, Netflix is selectively rebuilding features it once disrupted: live sports (NFL, MLB, tentpole events), scheduled programming, short-form video, podcasts, and third-party channels integrated directly into the app, while the ad tier reached 250 million monthly active users with expectations to double ad revenue to $3 billion in 2026. The strategic tension is stark—Netflix risks recreating the bloated television bundle it originally replaced, and despite capturing 7.8% of US TV time in April, YouTube reached a record 13.4% share by combining diverse content types, leaving Netflix needing to prove its broader strategy produces genuine engagement gains and durable returns on spending.
strategic_hook: Understanding Netflix's shift from pure content library to bundle-like service requires analyzing how customer needs have evolved (daily app usage versus occasional binge-watching) and mapping competitive threats from YouTube and free services to identify what content and features now drive retention and monetization.

heading: ENGLAND VS THE INTERNET: WHAT DID REDDIT MAKE OF THE NIGHT IT ALL FELL APART AGAINST ARGENTINA? (6 MINUTE READ)
summary: This article analyzes Reddit discussions from England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, examining how fans diagnosed the defeat and assigned blame in real time. The r/ThreeLions community quickly identified manager Tuchel's tactical substitutions at the hydration break—particularly removing attacking players for defenders—as the pivotal moment that shifted momentum, supported by possession statistics showing England had just 2 accurate passes in nearly 19 minutes after going ahead 1-0. The thread revealed a fanbase capable of sophisticated tactical analysis alongside emotional villainy-seeking, though a minority of commenters offered counterarguments, including that the collapse began before the substitutions and that player underperformance shared responsibility. Notably, the same community simultaneously conducted an unprompted apology campaign to full-back Djed Spence, whom fans had criticized pre-tournament but who performed well despite being injured in the play leading to Argentina's winning goal. The subreddit also demonstrated its moderation infrastructure actively removing brigading comments and xenophobic content, showing both the community's worst instincts and its capacity for self-policing.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: NETFLIX SAYS LIVE EVENTS BOLSTER ADS BUT AFFECT VIEWER ENGAGEMENT (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Netflix reported Q2 revenue growth of 13% year-over-year to $12.6 billion, driven by membership growth, pricing increases, and advertising momentum, with the company on track to double its 2025 ad revenue to $3 billion in 2026. The company is leveraging live events programming, particularly sports content including the Women's World Cup and expanded NFL games, to drive advertiser interest during upfront negotiations. However, Netflix acknowledged a tradeoff: while live events excel at driving acquisition and ad revenue through high viewer attention and premium pricing, they generate fewer total viewing hours compared to scripted content because they occupy limited broadcast windows. Executives also addressed investor concerns about softer viewer engagement, including declining viewing hours per member and audiences abandoning shows after a single season, attributing some of the slowdown to the strategic pivot toward live programming. Netflix is working to narrow monetization gaps between its ad-supported and ad-free tiers by expanding measurement capabilities, ad products, and its ad-tech stack.
strategic_hook: Netflix's strategic shift toward live events demonstrates how understanding the tradeoff between different content types—high monetization per event versus cumulative viewing hours—should inform both content acquisition strategy and advertiser value propositions during upfront sales.

heading: ZARA'S ‘DEATH PANTS' ARE TRENDING BECAUSE PEOPLE KEEP TRIPPING ON THEM (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Zara's "flowy wide leg pants," priced at $45.90, have become viral on social media as "death pants" because the floor-skimming, extra-wide fabric wraps around wearers' feet, causing them to trip and sustain injuries including broken wrists, fractured knees, and facial lacerations. Thousands of social media videos document users falling while wearing the pants, with influencers and customers sharing their injuries using hashtags like "Zara death trousers" and "deadly Zara pants." Fashion experts note that any loosely-designed pants pose similar hazards, but wide-leg trousers remain trendy for summer 2026 due to their cooling properties during heat waves, with Vogue calling them "one of those rare wardrobe staples that truly work for almost everyone." Zara has not made a public statement in response to the viral trend, though the company was contacted by CBC News.
strategic_hook: none.
